title: An honest machine learning research pipeline
brief:
You will build a small research pipeline in Python that trains a classification model on market data without letting the future leak into the past. At the end, it prints one honest report: the model's out-of-sample penalty against a coin flip, the positions it would take, and how fast its edge fades. The point is not a profitable model. The point is a pipeline whose numbers you can trust, so that a good result means something.

The pipeline has six parts, one for each lesson in this module:

1. **Point-in-time features** (`features.py`): a table of quarterly reports with a `published` date and revisions, and a function that returns each feature as it was known on a given date.
2. **Labels** (`labels.py`): triple-barrier labels with barriers at +5% and -5% and a horizon of 10 days, plus the end day of each label.
3. **A classification model** (`model.py`): logistic regression written with numpy and `scipy.optimize.minimize`, trained by making the average penalty `-log(p)` as small as possible.
4. **Purged cross-validation** (`cv.py`): 5 folds in time order, with training examples removed when their label days overlap a test fold, and an embargo of 5 days after it.
5. **Sizing from probability** (`sizing.py`): a quarter of Kelly on the edge `2p - 1`, divided by the 5% barrier and capped at 100% of equity, long or short.
6. **Signal decay** (`decay.py`): the information coefficient (a Spearman rank correlation) between the out-of-sample probability minus 0.5 and the return 1, 2, 3, 5 and 10 days later.

Generate the data yourself with numpy and a fixed seed, so every run gives the same numbers. Make 2,000 days of made-up prices for one share. Plant a weak, fading signal in them: a hidden series that keeps 70% of its value each day and moves the next day's return a little. Make a quarterly sales table whose figures are published 25 days after each quarter ends, and revise one figure 2 months after it is published. One feature comes from the price (the past 5-day return) and one from the sales table (sales growth as it was known on each day).

Constraints: Python 3.10 or later, with numpy, pandas, scipy and pytest only. No scikit-learn, no downloaded data and no network calls. Every number in the report must come from the pipeline, never typed in by hand. Each test result must come only from test folds.

starter.note: make_prices(seed) returns a DataFrame of 2,000 daily closes with a planted fading signal; make_reports(seed) returns quarterly sales with quarter, published and sales columns, including one revision.

growth_as_of(reports, date) keeps rows published on or before the date and the newest version of each quarter; build_features(prices, reports) returns one row per day with past_5d_return and sales_growth.
triple_barrier(close, horizon=10, barrier=0.05) returns a DataFrame with label (+1, -1 or 0) and end_day for each day that has a full horizon ahead.
fit(X, y) returns the starting value and one slope per feature; predict_proba(params, X) returns the probability of up; penalty(params, X, y) is the average -log(p).
purged_folds(n, end_day, k=5, embargo=5) yields (train_idx, test_idx) pairs; a training example is dropped when its days from t to end_day[t] touch the test fold.
Runs the whole pipeline: features, labels, purged cross-validation, sizing from the out-of-sample probabilities, and the IC at each later day. Prints the report.
test_features.py, test_labels.py, test_cv.py and test_sizing.py, with the small hand-checked cases from the lessons.

hints: Build and test each part on a tiny case you can check by hand before you run it on 2,000 days. The lessons' examples make good first tests.
Labels for the last 10 days have no full horizon. Drop those days from the examples, and drop the rows with missing features at the start too.
Logistic regression only has a label of up or not up. Use 1 for a +1 label and 0 for a -1 or 0 label, and say so in the report.

In purged_folds, compute each test fold's first day and the largest end_day of its examples. Drop every training example t with t <= that end day and end_day[t] >= the first day, then drop the next 5 days.
Collect the probabilities from each test fold into one series in day order. Size and measure the IC from that series only, never from probabilities on training days.
Compare the purged result with a plain cross-validation that removes nothing. If the plain one scores better, the difference is the leak the purge removed.

rubric.criterion: Sales growth on each day uses only reports published on or before that day, in the version known then, and a test shows the revision changes growth only after its publish date
Triple-barrier labels record which barrier is touched first and the day it is touched, and no label is used as a feature
The model is trained by minimising the average -log(p) and the report compares its test penalty with the coin flip's 0.693
Every fold drops the training examples whose label days overlap the test fold plus a 5-day embargo, and a test checks the training sizes for a small case
Positions come from out-of-sample probabilities only, grow with the distance from 0.5 and never pass 100% of equity
The report prints the information coefficient at 1, 2, 3, 5 and 10 days and says how many days of delay halve it

milestones.title: Point-in-time features and labels
milestones.body: Write data.py, features.py and labels.py. Test that growth_as_of gives 5.26% on 15 May 2024 and 14.58% on 15 August 2024 for the lesson's four reports. Test that the 11-price path from the labels lesson gives +1 on day 5 with barriers at 4% and a horizon of 10 days.

milestones.title: Logistic regression with purged folds
milestones.body: Write model.py and cv.py. Test that 100 examples with a horizon of 10, 5 folds and an embargo of 5 give training sizes of 65, 55, 55, 55 and 70. Then train on each fold's training rows and print the average test penalty next to 0.693.
milestones.checkCmd: python -m pytest tests/test_cv.py -q && python research.py --step model

milestones.title: Sizing from the out-of-sample probabilities
milestones.body: Write sizing.py. Test that probabilities of 0.50, 0.55, 0.60, 0.70 and 0.45 give positions of 0%, +50%, +100%, +100% and -50%. Size every day from the test-fold probabilities and print the share of days that are long, flat and short.
milestones.checkCmd: python -m pytest tests/test_sizing.py -q && python research.py --step sizing

milestones.title: The full report with signal decay
milestones.body: Write decay.py and finish research.py. Print the information coefficient at 1, 2, 3, 5 and 10 days, the first day on which it falls to half of day 1 or below, and the purged test penalty next to a plain cross-validation that removes nothing.
